Le joueur de roulette russe qui survit à un tirage n’a pas découvert de stratégie d’espérance positive.

The Russian-roulette player who survives one pull has not discovered a positive-expectancy strategy.

📚A system that wins only 40% of the time can still be profitable.

If winners average 2.5R and losers cost 1R, expectancy is (0.4 × 2.5) − (0.6 × 1) = 0.4R per trade.

Van Tharp shows reliability is secondary to the distribution of R-multiples; a high win rate with tiny gains and rare large losses produces negative expectancy.

The edge exists only while you remain in the game long enough for the average to appear. ✍️🏼
